provenance: Owner-supplied TLWH_Computer_Restoration_Codex_Handoff.md, section 6; reproduced from the canonical story attached to issue #46. Spoken text and directions are locked. Repair quantities are separately overridden to 4 Plates + 4 Rods.

inspection.speaker: dave
inspection.text: I've got some materials together. Tell me what you need.

inspection.speaker: computer
inspection.text: Core restoration requires four Ferrite Plates and four Ferrite Rods.

inspection.speaker: dave
inspection.text: All right. I'll see what I can do.

operational.speaker: computer
operational.text: Core systems operational. Manufacturing capability remains our immediate limitation.

cues.text: The screen fades in. Computer's restored display flickers, then stabilizes. A low electronic hum replaces the silence.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Core systems restored. Multiple subsystems remain offline.
A brief pause.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Dave? Are you receiving me?

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Yeah. I'm here.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Your biometrics indicate elevated stress and physical exhaustion.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: You should've seen me yesterday.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: I am unable to account for the time I was offline. How long has it been?

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Long enough.
Computer's display flickers briefly.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: I see. Your efforts to restore my systems have not gone unnoticed, Dave.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Don't thank me yet. We've still got a long way to go.
Dave looks toward the damaged ship interior.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: I need a full damage assessment. Everything. Tell me what it'll take to get this ship home.
Computer's display changes as diagnostic data begins scrolling across the screen.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Initiating ship-wide diagnostic. Stand by.
A brief pause. Several damaged systems appear on the display.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Hull integrity is compromised. Primary propulsion is offline. Navigation and long-range communications are unavailable.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: So we're not going anywhere.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Not in the ship's present condition.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: What can we fix?

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: The structural damage is manageable with sufficient materials. Restoring propulsion will be considerably more difficult.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Difficult how?

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Several critical components are beyond repair. They will need to be manufactured.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: I've got a Fabricator running outside.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: That is encouraging. Unfortunately, its present capabilities are insufficient for the components we require.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Then we improve them.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: That would be the logical course of action.
The diagnostic display pauses. A navigation record briefly appears among the damaged system reports.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Dave. There is an irregularity in the surviving navigation records.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: What kind of irregularity?

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Our final recorded course correction does not correspond with the assigned trajectory.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Could be damage from the crash.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: That is possible. Several records are incomplete. I cannot determine whether the discrepancy predates the impact.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Then we'll deal with it when we can. Right now, I need this ship flying.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Understood. I will preserve the available records for further analysis.
The navigation report disappears. Computer returns to the ship's damage assessment.
Computer's display returns to the ship-wide diagnostic summary. Several critical systems remain marked offline.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: All right. Where do we start?

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Our immediate limitation is manufacturing capability. The components required to restore propulsion exceed the tolerances of your current equipment.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: So the Fabricator needs work.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: Correct. We will need to determine which modifications are possible with the resources available to us.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: And after that?

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: We repair what we can. Restore the systems necessary for flight. Then we determine whether a return journey is possible.
Dave studies the damaged ship interior for a moment.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: It has to be possible.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: I cannot promise that, Dave.
A brief pause.

cues.speaker: computer
cues.text: But I can help you find out.

cues.speaker: dave
cues.text: Then let's get to work.
Computer's display settles into a stable operational state. The cutscene ends and control returns to the player.
